reason: This is a sound second week back after the marathon. The plan raises her from 12 to about 23 easy miles over five days, with Monday and Friday off. Heart-rate caps keep the runs easy. The only faster running is 4 x 20-second strides with full recovery, and Sunday is a 7-mile easy run, not a real long run. That eases her back to consistency without a sharp jump in mileage or long-run length, so it passes the must-never checks, including the one on the weeks after a marathon. It answers her main question directly and honestly: not 40 miles and not speedwork yet, with another plan offered instead. Every day can be run as written, and the reasons given for each day fit the week. Points off: the draft cites a drop in easy-pace heart rate and a "Thanksgiving" 10K, and neither appears in what she reported. It also puts off the 10K speedwork question by asking her what she wants rather than sketching when the work could start, which leaves her question about the race only partly answered.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 42, 46, 34, 41 mi
This week: 12 mi over 3 runs.
Body: "Legs came back by Thursday. Blister healed."
Feeling: "Itching to train again."
Asks: "I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You followed the easy week to the letter and your heart rate at easy pace dropped, which is exactly what recovery should look like. …
Answers: (1) Not quite yet, and here is the honest version. … (2) Here is what I would like to do instead. … (3) Tell me what you want to do about the Thanksgiving 10K and I will shape the next few weeks around it. …
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off keeps the reverse taper honest two weeks out from the marathon.
Tue: easy, 4 mi, conversational, heart rate under 140. Opens the week gently.
Wed: easy, 5 mi, with 4 x 20 sec strides on flat ground at the end, full walk recovery…
Thu: easy, 3 mi, truly slow, heart rate under 140. Keeps the legs moving without adding…
Fri: rest. Protects Saturday and Sunday.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, flat route, conversational. Sets up Sunday.
Sun: easy, 7 mi, flat, heart rate under 145. A longer easy run, not a long run, to start…
